## Sep 18 Performance Analysis

The model posted a 10-5 record (66.7% accuracy) on Thursday's slate, which represents a solid performance above baseline expectations. More importantly, the underlying process metrics held firm—our high-confidence picks (>60% win probability) converted at a 71.4% clip, suggesting proper calibration between projected and realized outcomes.

## Key Takeaways from Thursday's Slate

The misses came predominantly in mid-probability bands (54-59%), which aligns with expected variance in tight matchups. The Cubs-Reds outcome represented a true coin flip decided by late-game bullpen sequencing. The Rays miss was more concerning from a process standpoint—Tampa Bay's platoon disadvantage against the White Sox lineup was underweighted in our pre-game projections.

Our highest-conviction play, the Braves at 63%, cashed comfortably as Atlanta's lineup posted a .389 wOBA against Houston's bullpen arms. This validates the model's ability to identify exploitable matchup disparities in run-expectancy frameworks.

## Sep 19 Top Pick: Tigers at White Sox

For Friday's slate, our highest-value opportunity resides in the Tigers-White Sox rematch. Detroit checks in at 58% win probability, driven primarily by the pitching matchup and underlying team metrics.

**Pitching Edge:** Jackson Jobe takes the ball for Detroit with a 3.42 xFIP and elite strikeout stuff (28.4 K%). Sean Burke counters for Chicago with pedestrian peripherals—his 4.67 xFIP and 1.38 WHIP suggest continued struggles limiting baserunners. The gap in expected run prevention alone accounts for approximately 0.7 runs of projected value.

**Offensive Context:** Detroit's lineup has posted a 104 wRC+ over the last 30 days against right-handed pitching, while Chicago's offense ranks 28th in baseball with an 81 wRC+ in the same split. The run-expectancy matrix heavily favors the visiting Tigers in this context.

**Situational Factors:** Chicago's bullpen has been taxed recently (4.2 IP average over the last three games), creating potential late-game leverage advantages for Detroit's fresher relief corps.

## Expected Value Framework

At 58% implied probability, the Tigers represent positive expected value against typical market lines. Our models suggest fair odds closer to -140, while early market positioning may offer inefficiencies in the -125 to -135 range. The 0.7-run pitching differential combined with offensive splits creates a measurable edge worth exploiting.

As always, we're betting on process over outcomes. A 58% win probability means we expect this pick to lose 42% of the time—that's the nature of probabilistic forecasting. What matters is consistent identification of positive-EV spots across large sample sizes.
